commandSets.name: Energy Display
notes: When its Synchronize button, the owner's manual's Refresh/OK button, is pressed, the display sends Get iMeter Status (cmd1 0x82, cmd2 0x00) to each linked meter or modem, then stays awake for 3 seconds. Programming it needs stay awake on (cmd2 0x06) within those 3 seconds. A modem answers with the iMeter's reply, CRC included.

Every 3 minutes the display checks the temperature; when it has changed by more than 1 degree Celsius, it broadcasts cmd1 0x6E to group 4 (flags 0x8F, To 00 00 04) with the temperature in half degrees Celsius in cmd2. The Energy Display Developer Notes' example frame ends with one more byte, 0x1A, which they don't explain.
Here cmd1 0x2F with cmd2 0x01 reads and writes the meter in each group, not the ALL-Link database.
The Energy Display Developer Notes don't say whether the extended Sets carry a checksum.
The Energy Display 2448A2 Owner's Manual gives 10 cents a kilowatt-hour as the default cost.

commandSets.name: EZFlora
notes: Every Sprinkler Control sub-command's acknowledgment carries the valve status byte. For an invalid valve or program, ON commands return 0x00 and OFF commands 0xFF.

Status Changed broadcast (cmd1 0x27): with Enable Valve Status Change Message, the EZFlora broadcasts when a valve turns on or off during a program, but not after a direct valve command; with Enable Meter Count Change Message, it broadcasts when the meter count changes. The To Address carries the status byte in its high byte and the meter count's high and low bytes in its middle and low bytes.

The EZFlora answers an ID Request with an acknowledgment and a SET Button Pressed broadcast, and a Ping (cmd1 0x0F) with an acknowledgment. Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) is the same as holding the SET button 4 seconds, and Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) as holding it 10 seconds. ALL-Link Recall (cmd1 0x11, an ALL-Link command) recalls groups 0 to 15.
Configuration register bit 2 isn't documented. Bit 7 of the register and bit 6 of the valve status byte both show the pump option.

X10: units 1 to 8 turn valves 1 to 8 on and off; units 9 to 12 start and stop programs 1 to 4; unit 13 On inhibits commands and Off resumes them; unit 14 On skips forward and Off skips back; unit 16 On enables the pump on V8 and Off disables it.

The accessory connector (RJ-45) isn't for data: pin 1 input 1 (not used), pin 2 +5 V auxiliary (50 mA maximum), pins 3, 5 and 7 ground, pin 4 water meter pulse input (with a built-in pull-up), pin 6 rain sensor (must be pulled up to inhibit), pin 8 no connection.

commandSets.description: The EZSnsRF 5010E wireless sensor receiver from Compacta International, which turns Dakota Alert 3000-series transmitter codes into Insteon group commands: its code records, the buffer that loads and saves them, and Peek and Poke.
commandSets.name: EZSnsRF
notes: An Insteon group command is sent for a code whose record is in use and linked; a broadcast for a code whose record is only in use. The broadcast (Status Change, cmd1 0x27) carries the record number, 0x00 through 0x13, in cmd2 bits 0 to 5.

Code records: the device keeps a record for each code it has learned, 20 in all (0x00 through 0x13), and works on one at a time in the code record buffer. Specific Code Record Write (extended, cmd1 0xF2, cmd2 the record) writes D1 through D8 to a record. A record's 8 bytes: flags (bit 7 in use, bit 6 has an Insteon link, bits 0 to 4 the timer), the code's low byte, the code's high byte (4 bits used), the Insteon group (1 to 20), then cmd1 and cmd2 sent when the signal turns on and cmd1 and cmd2 sent when it turns off.

The EZSnsRF Insteon Messages/Commands give the record's timer in 0.5-second steps; the Quick-Start Guide EZSnsRF Wireless Sensor Receiver Model #5010E adds half a minute for each tap of the SET button, for 0.5 to 15.5 minutes.
Peek and Poke addresses, with Set Address MSB 0x00: 0x00 configuration (r), 0x02 firmware revision (r), 0x03 EEPROM loaded (r), 0x04 to 0x0B the code record buffer (rw).
The device answers an ID Request with an acknowledgment and a SET Button Pressed broadcast, without entering linking mode.
Its Poke description says to follow a Poke with Load EEPROM from RAM, which its command table doesn't list.
sources: Quick-Start Guide EZSnsRF Wireless Sensor Receiver Model #5010E

commandSets.description: The EZX10RF 5010G X10 RF transceiver and Insteon scene controller from Compacta International, which turns X10 addresses into Insteon group commands: its code records, the buffer that loads and saves them, the X10 address filter and Peek and Poke.
commandSets.name: EZX10RF
notes: An Insteon group command is sent for an X10 address whose record is in use and linked; a broadcast for one whose record is only in use. The broadcast (Status Change, cmd1 0x27) carries the record number, 0x00 through 0x13, in cmd2 bits 0 to 5, and the X10 command in bits 6 and 7: 00 Off, 01 Dim, 10 On, 11 Bright.

Code records: the device keeps a record for each code it has learned, 20 in all (0x00 through 0x13), and works on one at a time in the code record buffer. Specific Code Record Write (extended, cmd1 0xF2, cmd2 the record) writes D1 through D8 to a record. A record's 8 bytes: flags (bit 7 in use, bit 6 has an Insteon link, bits 0 to 4 the timer), the X10 house and unit code, the X10 command (not used), the Insteon group (1 to 20), then cmd1 and cmd2 sent when the signal turns on and cmd1 and cmd2 sent when it turns off.

The EZX10RF Insteon Messages/Commands give the record's timer in 0.5-second steps; the Quick-Start Guide EZX10RF Wireless Sensor Receiver Insteon EZX10RF—Model #5010G adds half a minute for each tap of the SET button, for 0.5 to 15.5 minutes.

Peek and Poke addresses, with Set Address MSB 0x00: 0x00 the last X10 house and unit code received (r), 0x01 the last X10 command received (r), 0x02 firmware revision (r), 0x03 EEPROM loaded (r), 0x04 to 0x23 the X10 address filter, 16 by 16 bits, 0x24 to 0x2B the code record buffer (rw). The EZX10RF Insteon Messages/Commands give these addresses without a prefix, as 04-35 and 36-43; read as decimal, they match the filter's 32 bytes and the buffer's 8.
The device answers an ID Request with an acknowledgment and a SET Button Pressed broadcast, without entering linking mode.
Its Poke description says to follow a Poke with Load EEPROM from RAM, which its command table doesn't list.
sources: Quick-Start Guide EZX10RF Wireless Sensor Receiver Insteon EZX10RF—Model #5010G

commandSets.name: EZIOxx
notes: The EZIOxx Advanced Details (Rev 2.3, 2016) apply to firmware 2.0 and above. They give EZIO the category 0x07 and subcategory 0x02; Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) gives each model its own subcategory.

Each input sends a group command when it changes, to the group stored for it at addresses 0x40 through 0x47 (inputs 1 to 8), which needn't match the input's number; several inputs can share a group. An input that isn't linked sends a broadcast instead, when broadcasts are enabled. The commands sent on the off-to-on and on-to-off transitions default to Insteon On and Off and can be changed, at addresses 0x20 through 0x3F.

An input can have a timer, 1 second to 255 minutes, that starts when the input turns on and sends the on-to-off command when it runs out; the device can ignore the input turning off while the timer runs. An input can also switch its corresponding output directly (the inputs-to-outputs crosslink at address 0x1A).

Inputs are digital, analog or 1-Wire (one DS18B20 temperature sensor). An analog or 1-Wire input reads as on while its value is past its alarm point; its off-to-on and on-to-off alarm points are separate counts from 0 to 1023, which gives it hysteresis. Analog inputs read 0 to 5 V or 0 to 3.3 V depending on the model.

Besides the Configuration Port, software can set a Configuration Register: Enable Analog Inputs, Continuous A/D Conversion (once a second rather than when read), Debounce the Inputs, Enable 1-W Sensor, Set Timers in Seconds and Broadcast on Status Change.

As a responder, the device reads the middle and lower data bytes of its ALL-Link database record when a group On arrives: it turns on one output, sets or turns on a pattern of outputs (the snapshot taken when the link was made), or triggers one of its inputs as if it had turned on, which then sends that input's group command if the input is linked. With output timers enabled, an output turns off when its timer runs out, for pulses as short as 1 second.

Status Changed broadcast (cmd1 0x27): when broadcasts are enabled, the device sends the output or input port's byte in cmd2 when it changes, with 00 in the To Address's low byte for the output port and 01 for the input port.
The device answers an ID Request with an acknowledgment and a SET Button Pressed broadcast, without entering linking mode. ALL-Link Recall (cmd1 0x11, an ALL-Link command) recalls groups 0 to 15.

Peek and Poke addresses, with Set Address MSB 0x00: 0x00 to 0x07 output timers (rw); 0x08 X10 house code (rw); 0x09 Configuration Port (rw); 0x0A to 0x11 sensor 1 to 4 alarms, 2 bytes each (rw); 0x12 to 0x19 analog inputs 1 and 2 alarms, 4 bytes each (rw); 0x1A inputs-to-outputs crosslink bitmap (rw); 0x1B to 0x1F reserved; 0x20 to 0x3F the group command on/off sequence for inputs 1 to 8 (rw); 0x40 to 0x47 group numbers for inputs 1 to 8 (rw); 0x48 firmware version (r); 0x49 EEPROM loaded flag (r); 0x4A output port status (r); 0x4B input port status (r); 0x4C analog data, 2 bytes for each of 2 inputs (r); 0x50 1-Wire raw data (r); 0x58 to 0x5F input timers (rw). A Poke to an rw location lasts once Update EEPROM saves it.

X10: units 1 to 8 turn outputs 1 to 8 on and off, and unit 16 On and Off enable and disable the output timers. To enable X10, pick a house code (A to P) on an X10 controller, hold the SET button at least 4 seconds and release it so the LED blinks, then send 3 On commands (any unit) until the LED stops blinking; 3 Off commands disable it. The Quick-Start Guide EZIO2X4—Model #5010D—2-Relay/4-Input Controller and the Quick-Start Guide EZIO4O—Model #5010J—4-Relay Load Controller give one On or Off command instead of 3.

notes: The FanLinc Developer Notes give the ramp rate Set's range as 0x00 through 0x1F, 0.1 second to 2 seconds, but its own ramp rate table runs from 0x01 (8 minutes) to 0x1F (0.1 second), with 0x00 at 2 seconds.
The FanLinc Developer Notes fill the rest of its fan commands and extended Sets with 0x00 and doesn't mention a checksum in D14.
The FanLinc Developer Notes say that its fan off command also turns the light off on the firmware it describes.
The FanLinc Developer Notes mark bit 0 of the 0x05 reply reserved and doesn't list Set Operating Flags 0x10, 0x11 or 0x14 through 0x19; another source gives them for the KeypadLinc code base.
The FanLinc Developer Notes control the light, group 1, as a KeypadLinc dimmer's load, and the fan, group 2, with extended commands.

notes: Ramp rate 0x00 is 2 seconds, 0x01 8 minutes, 0x0A 2 minutes, 0x0D 47 seconds, 0x13 28 seconds, 0x18 8.5 seconds, 0x1B 2 seconds, 0x1C 0.5 second and 0x1F 0.1 second.

The device ignores or rejects any command its documents don't list, Product Data Request (cmd1 0x03) among them. Besides the commands here, they list the linking commands, Get Insteon Engine Version, ID Request and ALL-Link database reads, writes and modifies.

Its database layout gives records from 0x0FFF down to 0x0300, 416 of them; the database read reply gives addresses from 0x0FFF to 0x0407. Bit 0 of a record's flags is fast fail, bit 2 marks a Lighting Director record, bits 3 and 4 hold its hop count and bit 5 is always 1; the device may change some of these bits on its own.
The load settings reply (readLoadSettings) starts with the same bytes as the extended Get reply, so wait for one before asking for the other.
The extended Get request carries no checksum.

commandSets.name: i3 Keypad
notes: Ramp rate 0x00 is 2 seconds, 0x01 8 minutes, 0x0A 2 minutes, 0x0D 47 seconds, 0x13 28 seconds, 0x18 8.5 seconds, 0x1B 2 seconds, 0x1C 0.5 second and 0x1F 0.1 second.

The device ignores or rejects any command its documents don't list, Product Data Request (cmd1 0x03) among them. Besides the commands here, they list the linking commands, Get Insteon Engine Version, ID Request and ALL-Link database reads, writes and modifies.

Its database layout gives records from 0x0FFF down to 0x0300, 416 of them; the database read reply gives addresses from 0x0FFF to 0x0407. Bit 0 of a record's flags is fast fail, bit 2 marks a Lighting Director record, bits 3 and 4 hold its hop count and bit 5 is always 1; the device may change some of these bits on its own.
The load settings reply (readLoadSettings) starts with the same bytes as the extended Get reply, so wait for one before asking for the other.
D14 of the extended Get reply is the group mask, not a checksum, and the Get request carries no checksum.
Bit 4 of operating flags query 0x05, set and cleared with cmd2 0x19 and 0x18, locks the buttons here; on the KeypadLinc it asks for checksums.
The extended Set also takes selector 0x11, LED flags, per group, which the documents don't describe.

commandSets.name: i3 Paddle
notes: Ramp rate 0x00 is 2 seconds, 0x01 8 minutes, 0x0A 2 minutes, 0x0D 47 seconds, 0x13 28 seconds, 0x18 8.5 seconds, 0x1B 2 seconds, 0x1C 0.5 second and 0x1F 0.1 second.

The device ignores or rejects any command its documents don't list, Product Data Request (cmd1 0x03) among them. Besides the commands here, they list the linking commands, Get Insteon Engine Version, ID Request and ALL-Link database reads, writes and modifies.

Its database layout gives records from 0x0FFF down to 0x0300, 416 of them; the database read reply gives addresses from 0x0FFF to 0x0407. Bit 0 of a record's flags is fast fail, bit 2 marks a Lighting Director record, bits 3 and 4 hold its hop count and bit 5 is always 1; the device may change some of these bits on its own.
The load settings reply (readLoadSettings) starts with the same bytes as the extended Get reply, so wait for one before asking for the other.
The extended Get request carries no checksum.

The In-Line 0-10VDC Dimmer Developer Notes mark bit 2 of the 0x00 reply and bits 2 and 4 of the 0x05 reply N/A and lists no Set Operating Flags for resume dim, error blink or the checksum flag, so they're left out here; another source gives them for the KeypadLinc code base.

The In-Line 0-10VDC Dimmer Developer Notes list the input groups in D1 of the DAC range and retry Sets as well, but doesn't say whether the device keeps them per group.
The second Get's reply has the same cmd2 and D2 as the first's, so a reply is told apart only by the request it answers.
The In-Line 0-10VDC Dimmer Developer Notes list no status request; Insteon's 2007 command tables give cmd1 0x19 for every dimmer.

commandSets.name: KeypadLinc
notes: Earlier sources give ramp rates 0x00 through 0x1F as 9 minutes down to 0.1 second; the later ones make 0x01 8 minutes and 0x00 2 seconds.

Earlier sources, the Insteon Developer's Guide and the KeypadLinc Line Developer Notes give D14 of the reply as the trigger mask; later sources moved the trigger mask to query 0x08 and use D14 for the radio group mask.
The Insteon Developer's Guide sets selectors 0x08 through 0x0C one button at a time; other sources write the whole mask.
The KeypadLinc Line Developer Notes cover firmware 0x41 and later of subcategories 0x1B, 0x1C, 0x0F, 0x1E and 0x2C, and every firmware of 0x41 and 0x42.
In the 6-button layout, the On and Off buttons are group 1 and the four small buttons groups 3 through 6; in the 8-button layout, the buttons are groups 1 through 8.

With the load detached, group 9 controls the load: cmd1 0x19 with cmd2 0x00 reads its level, D11 of the extended Get reply holds the LEDs of groups 1 through 8, a group 1 On or Off sets the group 1 LEDs, and the LED mask Set sets the others.

To make buttons act as radio buttons, set both the on mask and the off mask of each button to the other buttons in the group, and link each button as a controller with an off-only link (on-level 0x00) to the devices the other buttons control.

commandSets.name: KeypadLinc Schedule Timer
notes: Insteon's documents don't say which Get Operating Flags bit each Set Operating Flags command changes on this keypad.
A Get with 0x01 in D3 returns the on and off times of group D1 in D3 through D10, and a Get with 0x02 in D3 returns the time of day in D3 through D6, in the layout the Sets use.
Earlier sources give ramp rates 0x00 through 0x1F as 9 minutes down to 0.1 second; the later ones make 0x01 8 minutes and 0x00 2 seconds.
Earlier sources and the Insteon Developer's Guide give D14 of the reply as the trigger mask; later sources moved the trigger mask to query 0x08 and use D14 for the radio group mask.
The Insteon Developer's Guide sets selectors 0x08 through 0x0C one button at a time; other sources write the whole mask.

commandSets.name: LED Bulb
notes: When it powers up, the bulb sends a SET button broadcast and stays in responder linking mode for 5 seconds; with programming lock on, it doesn't enter linking mode. To link it, put the controller in linking mode, then power the bulb up.
The bulb's levels differ from other dimmers': at 0x0F it gives about a tenth of its full light, and at 0x7F more than half.
The LED Bulb Developer Notes give ramp rate 0x00 as about 2 seconds when setting it and as 9 minutes in their ramp table; the rest of the table runs from 8 minutes at 0x01 to 0.1 second at 0x1F.
Of the extended Get reply, the LED Bulb Developer Notes use only D7, the ramp rate.

notes: The sensors sleep to save their batteries, and hear commands only while awake.
Direct commands from a device that isn't in the sensor's ALL-Link database get a NAK with 0xFF in cmd2.
The Open/Close Sensor's configuration byte is 0x43 by default, and the Leak Sensor's is 0x4F.
The guides give D4 and D5 of the extended Get reply as 0x01 and 0x23 without saying what they hold.
The guides document no Set Operating Flags commands for these sensors. Write the configuration byte with an extended Set instead.

commandSets.name: Outdoor ApplianceLinc, firmware 0x42
notes: The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes mark the Get Operating Flags 0x00 reply N/A. Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: it answered, and the device looks only at bit 0 of cmd2. An odd cmd2 answers with the ALL-Link database delta. An even cmd2 answers with the operating flags ORed with cmd2: with the flags at 0x42, cmd2 0x00 and 0x02 read 0x42, 0x04 read 0x46, 0x08 read 0x4A, 0x10 read 0x52, 0x20 read 0x62 and 0x80 read 0xC2. So query with cmd2 0x00 for the flags and 0x01 for the delta.
Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: bits 2 to 5 and bit 7 of the flags always read 0.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: before any change, the flags read 0x42: programming lock off, LED on transmit on and key beep off. The device was secondhand, so these may not be its factory settings, and the catalog gives no defaults.

It sends Set Operating Flags as extended messages with a checksum in D14. Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: error blink (0x14, 0x15) and cleanup report (0x16, 0x17) were acknowledged, but no Get Operating Flags reply and no byte of the extended Get reply changed, so they stay flag commands with no bit.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: the extended Get reply's data stayed 0x01 0x01 0x0F 0xEF 0x00 0x00 0x1C 0xFE 0x20 0x00 0x00 0x01 0x26 0xD1 through every flag change. D3 and D4 (0x0F 0xEF), D9 (0x20) and D12 and D13 (0x01 0x26) aren't explained by any document.
The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes give no extended Set for the settings its Get reports.

The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes say the device sends its Assign to ALL-Link Group broadcast on power-up and supports only responder links, whose on-level should be 0xFE and ramp rate 0x1F. Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: holding its SET button made it the controller of group 1, but tapping the button sent no group commands over that link.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: the device writes its own responder record when it's linked remotely, with Start ALL-Linking on the modem and Enter Linking Mode sent to the device, and doesn't use the 0xFE and 0x1F above. After one such link, as responder to a Hub 2245's group 0, its record held Data 1 to 3 as 0xFF 0x00 0x00; after a later one, 0x00 0x00 0x00, and with on-level 0x00 an On to group 0 from the modem left the load off.

The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes give the device's identity as category 0x01 and subcategory 0x3A, which the catalog gives to the 2672 LED bulb; the catalog keeps 0x02 and 0x38 for the 2634-222.

commandSets.name: Siren
notes: Responder groups 1, 3 and 5 trigger the alert when the siren is armed away, home or either; groups 2, 4 and 6 arm it away, home or both. A group On (cmd1 0x11) to an arm group starts a 45-second countdown, which beeps each second unless the link makes it silent, Fast On (cmd1 0x12) starts it silently, and another arm group during the countdown changes the mode without restarting it. A group Off (cmd1 0x13) to any arm group disarms the siren and silences it. The Siren Module Developer Notes' description of arming says Fast Off arms silently; their group commands and the Siren 2868-222 Owner's Manual give Fast On.
While it's arming, linked devices don't trigger the alert. Sending the arm group again, or Off, cancels arming.
While the alert sounds, the siren broadcasts Fast On and Fast Off (cmd1 0x12 and 0x14) to group 1 in turn, every 2 seconds.

An alert record's data holds the delay and duration, the alert type and a record type; an arm record's data holds a record type. The Siren Module Developer Notes also say linking to an arm group stores the countdown behavior.
The siren adds or modifies a record with ALL-Link database command D2 0x03, matching on group and ID, and answers 0x2F with NAK 0xF9 when its database is full.

Mode reports use a different table from the mode the thermostat keeps. Earlier sources give the kept table for mode reports; later sources, used here, give a table of its own.
Insteon's later documents don't list reads with cmd1 0x6A, or with cmd1 0x6B and cmd2 0x02 or 0x03, for the TempLinc. Read its state with readStatus or readSettings instead.
The TempLinc's Get Operating Flags reply isn't documented; read its settings from readSettings.
Insteon's documents don't give the units of the first page's own temperature, the zone temperatures, or the external temperature report, cmd1 0x73.
Earlier sources read the extended Get with the temperature in D3 and D4, and a second page chosen by D2 0x10; later sources, used here, choose pages by D3.
Extended Get and Set take 0x01 in D1; other values are also accepted.

notes: A neutral wire is required. 100 to 277VAC, 50/60Hz, on a circuit protected by a 20A or smaller breaker or fuse.
In a multi-gang box the dimmer is derated by 200W for each immediately adjacent dimmer.

In 3-way and multi-way circuits every switch must be replaced by a keypad or SwitchLinc. Connect line and one traveler to the first keypad's black wire and cap its red wire; at the load box connect the same traveler to black and the load to red; at middle boxes join the two black travelers to black and cap the red wire; cap all unused travelers. Then cross-link the keypads so they all control the load.

Connect the keypad's bare copper wire to ground, white to neutral, red to load and black to line. Make sure the connections are firm with no exposed wire.

devices.name: 2-Wire Dimmer Switch
notes: Needs no neutral wire.
Repeats RF but not powerline.
In the SwitchLinc 2-Wire Dimmer Developer Notes, Set Operating Flags cmd2 0x0C to 0x0F repeat the LED on transmit and resume dim settings, and 0x10, 0x11 and 0x18 to 0x1D aren't used.

When its SET button is held, the dimmer broadcasts cmd1 0x01 with its category, subcategory and firmware in the To address; holding it again, to unlink, sends cmd1 0x02. The SwitchLinc 2-Wire Dimmer Developer Notes' example uses flags 0xCF and cmd2 0x01, the group; the Insteon Developer's Guide gives flags 0x8F and cmd2 0xFF, and makes cmd1 0x02 a controller's SET button rather than unlinking. An ID Request (cmd1 0x10) gets the same cmd1 0x01 broadcast with cmd2 0x00.

The SwitchLinc 2-Wire Dimmer Developer Notes list no operating flags readings 0x02 to 0x04, no bits 6 and 7 in the 0x00 reply, no X10 bytes in the extended Get reply, and no X10 address or retries writes, though they keep the X10 disable and enable commands and the 0x05 X10 bit.
The SwitchLinc 2-Wire Dimmer Developer Notes send D1 0x00 in the ramp rate and on-level Sets and say other values are ignored; the catalog's settings send 0x01, as for other products.

devices.name: Outdoor On/Off Plug
notes: Has no X10.
The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes give its identity as category 0x01 and subcategory 0x3A, which the catalog gives to the 2672.

Its owner's manual lists it as an Insteon controller; its Developer Notes list it as a responder only. Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: holding its SET button, with a modem in Start ALL-Linking as responder, linked it as the controller of group 1, but tapping its one button, which is also its SET button, switched the load and sent no group commands. The only message seen from it was SET Button Pressed (cmd1 0x01), when the button was held into linking mode. So a controller link can be made, but taps aren't reported, and an app learns its state only with Light Status Request. The catalog gives it the role responder, its practical behavior.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x42: when a Hub 2245 linked it remotely, as the responder to the Hub's group 0, the module itself wrote its responder record for that link with Data 1 to 3 as 0xFF 0x00 0x00; after a later remote link, the record held 0x00 0x00 0x00, and an On to group 0 from the modem left the load off. The Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes say to set the on-level to 0xFE and the ramp rate to 0x1F. Its controller record for group 1, to the Hub, held 0x03 0x00 0x00.
sources: Outdoor ApplianceLinc with RF Developer Notes
Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 Quick Start Guide

notes: HouseLinc names it Smoke Detector.

notes: Each relay is a switch rated 0.5 A at 30 V DC or 120 V AC, between terminals Rx_A and Rx_B. Timers can pulse a relay from 1 second to 255 minutes.

Inputs I1 and I2 are opto-isolated and need 3 to 30 V DC between their + and - terminals; for a dry contact, wire + to the +5 V terminal and the contact between - and GND. I3 and I4 are digital by default, on at 0 to 1 V DC and off at 3 to 5 V DC, and need a voltage, not a dry contact (a pull-up resistor to +5 V will do); software can set them to measure 0 to 5 V DC as a count from 0 to 1023 and alarm at set levels. The +5 V terminal supplies at most 20 mA.
Its ALL-Link database holds up to 30 links.

As a responder, a record whose Data 2 is 0x01 triggers the input in Data 3 (0x00 for input 1) as if it had turned on, so the input sends its own group command. Groups 1 and 2 are also relays 1 and 2, whose responder records the catalog gives for those groups; inputs 1 and 2 can be triggered the same way, with Data 3 0x00 or 0x01.

The Quick-Start Guide EZIO2X4—Model #5010D—2-Relay/4-Input Controller applies to firmware 2.2 and above. Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) records that 0x07/0x03 was first assigned to an EZIO3R I/O Module.

devices.name: EZIO8SA
notes: Neither the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA nor the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA & PLM Combo gives a model number; the profile is named for the product.
Outputs 7 and 8 are swapped: to control output 8, address output 7, and the other way around.

As a responder, a record whose Data 2 is 0x01 triggers the input in Data 3 (0x00 for input 1) as if it had turned on, so the input sends its own group command. The EZIOxx Advanced Details allow it for inputs 1 to 7, but neither the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA nor the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA & PLM Combo gives a way to link one, and groups 1 to 7 are also outputs 1 to 7, whose responder records the catalog gives for those groups.
An EZIComm 5010K connected to the PLM port in place of the modem doesn't power the EZIO8SA, so the EZIO8SA still needs its own DC adapter.
Each relay is Form C (SPDT), rated 3 A at 24 V DC or 120 V AC, with CM, NC and NO terminals. Output timers run from 1 to 255 seconds or minutes.

Inputs 1 to 4 (DI1 to DI4) are opto-isolated and need 3 to 30 V DC; a dry contact can use the 12 V DC terminal. Inputs 5 and 6 (Anl1, Anl2) are digital by default, on at 0 to 1 V DC and off at 2 to 3 V DC, or analog for 0 to 3 V DC sensors with trip points from 0 to 1023; ground them if unused, or they send constant Insteon traffic. Input 7 is 1-Wire, for a DS18B20 temperature sensor.
An EZEye light sensor on an analog input reads 1023 counts at about 3 V.
